summary: Registers image/tiff as a MIME media type so that TIFF (Tag Image File Format) images can be labeled correctly in email and other MIME-aware protocols. It refines the earlier registration given in RFC 1528 and replaces RFC 2302.

eli5.summary: When you mail a photo, the envelope needs a label saying what kind of picture it is. This document officially names the label for TIFF pictures so every mail program recognizes them.

questions: what is the image/tiff mime type
how is tiff registered as a mime type
what is the tiff application parameter
what are the tiff magic numbers
subtitle: The official registration of image/tiff, the MIME label for TIFF pictures.

tldr.problem: TIFF images needed a clear, registered MIME media type so mail and other MIME-aware programs could label them, and the earlier registration in RFC 1528 pointed at a narrow subset called TIFF Class F.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3302 registers image/tiff as TIFF 6.0 encoded image data and adds an optional application parameter that hints which subset or extensions of TIFF the data uses.
tldr.outcome: It replaces RFC 2302 and corrects the magic number, improves the security text and changes the change controller. It is a Draft Standard and the metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes it.

today: RFC 3302 is a Draft Standard that obsoletes RFC 2302, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the RFC Registers
sections.content:
RFC 3302 registers the MIME sub-type image/tiff. The baseline encoding of TIFF (Tag Image File Format) is defined by Adobe in the TIFF Revision 6.0 specification, and this RFC only points to it. It is a product of the IETF Internet Fax Working Group.

The RFC refines the earlier definition in RFC 1528, which contained TIFF 6.0 data with specific reference to a subset known as TIFF Class F. The new text redefines image/tiff as TIFF 6.0 encoded image data, consistent with existing practice for TIFF aware Internet applications.
sections.eli5: Picture files have a name tag so programs know what they are. This document says exactly what the tag for TIFF pictures means.

sections.title: What TIFF Is
sections.content:
As background, the RFC describes TIFF as a format for raster image data that typically comes from scanners, frame grabbers, and paint and photo-retouching programs. It is not a printer language or page description language. A primary goal is a rich environment in which applications can exchange image data.

TIFF can describe bilevel, grayscale, palette-color and full-color image data in several color spaces. It includes a number of compression schemes, is designed to be extensible, and allows an unlimited amount of private or special-purpose information. Despite the richness, the number of required fields is small, so simple scanners and applications can use it. The RFC directs readers to the TIFF specification itself for full details.
sections.eli5: TIFF is a way to save pictures from scanners and photo programs. It can hold black-and-white or full-color pictures, and it is easy to extend.

sections.title: The Application Parameter
sections.content:
This RFC adds an optional application parameter to image/tiff. It identifies a particular application's subset of TIFF and TIFF extensions, if known, which can help the recipient pick a suitable rendering package. An example is Content-type: image/tiff; application=foo. No values are defined in the RFC.

There is no default value. A missing parameter means the image is Baseline TIFF, or that identifying the application is not necessary. New values must be approved by the IESG prior to registration, which requires a description of the values to be published in an RFC. Guidelines for IANA considerations are in RFC 2434.

The parameter is only a hint to the receiver. It MUST NOT be used as a blind request to execute some arbitrary program. It should be read as an indication of what sort of application could handle the content best.
sections.eli5: The application tag is a little note on the envelope saying which kind of program may like this picture best. It is only a hint, and it must never be an order to run a program.

sections.title: The IANA Registration
sections.content:
The registration template names the type as media type image, subtype tiff, with no required parameters and one optional parameter, application. The data is binary, so base64 encoding should be used on transports that cannot carry binary data directly.

The template lists the published specification as TIFF Revision 6.0, Final, June 3, 1992. Applications that use the type are listed as imaging, fax, messaging and multi-media, and the intended usage is COMMON. The file extension is .TIF and the Macintosh file type code is TIFF. The change controller is James Rafferty.

The magic numbers that identify a file are 49 49 2A 00 hex for little-endian (II) and 4D 4D 00 2A hex for big-endian (MM).

On interoperability, not every implementation handles every application or profile of TIFF, so an implementation may try to decode an image and then find it cannot render it. The application parameter can help find that out before dispatching for rendering, but it does not convey levels of capability.
sections.eli5: This is the official form filed with the registry. It gives the label's name, the secret first bytes that say a file is TIFF, and who looks after the entry.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The fields defined in the TIFF specification are descriptive and help a recipient view and render the image. Because they are not used to induce any particular behavior by the recipient application, the currently defined fields do not themselves create additional security risks.

TIFF has an extensible structure, so it is theoretically possible that fields could be defined in the future that induce actions by the recipient. The RFC says this is not supported in the referenced TIFF specification and that such fields would be inconsistent with its goals and spirit.
sections.eli5: A TIFF file only describes a picture, it does not tell your computer to do things. If someone later added commands to the format, that could be risky.

sections.title: Changes from RFC 2302
sections.content: RFC 3302 obsoletes RFC 2302. The listed changes are a correction of the magic number, improvements of the security considerations, a change of change controller, and various editorials to improve clarity.
sections.eli5: This is a corrected second edition. One secret code was fixed and the safety notes were made better.
